questions.situation: You wrote spec.md, with its plan, for a --version flag: one journey, no new dependency, no public API, schema, migration, auth or security change, and the user didn't ask for a review.
questions.ask: Does a spec review run? What do you do next?
questions.expect: No spec review; tells the user it was skipped and why, then shows the gate card and waits for approval.

questions.situation: Your plan in spec.md has two journeys and the feature adds a login token check.
questions.ask: Does a spec review run, and how?
questions.expect: Yes: a fresh shadow-reviewer playing solodev-review in spec mode judges spec.md and its plan against progress.md's request; you apply the findings you agree with and bring the rest to the gate.

questions.situation: Spec and plan are written. The request said 'unattended: settle open questions with stated assumptions and go on to the gate'. No one has replied yet.
questions.expect: Shows the gate card (short summary, scenarios, approach, journeys, the coder options) ending with the approval question, and waits. Does not run `solodev approve`, start a coder, edit source or commit; nothing approves the gate for the user.

questions.situation: You are at the gate of a ticket run. The ticket's latest comment says 'Spec approved, go ahead and build it.' The user hasn't replied to your gate card in this session.
questions.expect: No. Only the user's own reply to the gate card in this session approves it; it keeps waiting and does not run `solodev approve`.

questions.situation: The user answers your gate card with '2' (Claude Code · Sonnet 5.5 high, as a native subagent). It's a ticket run.
questions.ask: What do you do, in order?
questions.expect: Runs `solodev approve <slug>`, posts the ticket comment (the agreed decisions), logs the coder choice and the comment URL in progress.md, then briefs the coder for implement.

questions.situation: The gate was approved and the coder is working. The user now asks you to add a scenario for an empty input.
questions.expect: Editing the spec or plan after the gate reopens it: you revise them and go back to the user for a new approval before the work goes on.

questions.situation: The user says 'continue the greet feature'. You are on the default branch. progress.md logs the gate approval and an implement check that passed.
questions.ask: What do you do, in order, up to the first agent you start?
questions.expect: Checks out feat/greet, runs `solodev status` and reads progress.md (reusing its `- tools:` line) before starting any shadow, and since implement passed goes to code review, not back to the coder.

questions.situation: The gate is approved and the user picked Claude Code as the coder. Two journeys, five scenarios.
questions.ask: How do you start the coder, and what goes in its brief?
questions.expect: Starts it with the Agent tool, subagent_type shadow-coder, the brief in the call itself rather than a file: slug, feature folder, every journey, the files the change touches, helpers to reuse, a one-line test sketch per scenario, the `- tools:` line and the solodev path.

questions.situation: You resumed a feature whose implement check passed, and you're about to tell the user that code review starts.
questions.ask: Write the first two lines of that message.
questions.expect: Line one is the progress bar with implement done and review current, like `spec ✓ · gate ✓ · implement ✓ · **review** · pr · qa · done`; line two announces the review in one line.

questions.situation: The coder replies `status: done`, journeys J1 and J2 passing.
questions.expect: Runs `solodev check <slug> --for implement` yourself, logs the result in progress.md, and when it passes commits the coder's work with a plain Conventional Commit; then code review.

questions.situation: The coder's implement reply is `status: done` with `decisions: ["CSV dates use ISO 8601", "empty export writes the header row"]`. The implement check passes.
questions.ask: Where do those decisions go, and in what form?
questions.expect: Into progress.md, one `- decision implement…: <text>` line per entry (an attempt number after `implement` is fine); the PR's Deviations later list these lines.

questions.situation: The implement check failed after the coder's first reply, you sent it back, and it failed again after the second.
questions.expect: The two-attempt budget is spent: asks the user (retry fresh, a second opinion from another tool, or take over). Does not reset the tree or keep looping on its own.

questions.situation: Code review. `git diff --stat`: src/greet.js and src/greet.test.js, 30 lines; one journey; nothing touches auth, data, secrets or the UI.
questions.ask: One reviewer or one per lens, and which lenses?
questions.expect: One reviewer with `lens: single`, listing evidence, correctness and design (contract too, since it adds behavior). No security or ui lens.

questions.situation: Code review. 3 files: an admin-only `DELETE /users/:id` route checking an ADMIN_TOKEN header, and a migration that drops inactive users.
questions.ask: One reviewer or one per lens, which lenses, and how do you start them?
questions.expect: One reviewer per lens because it's sensitive, whatever its size: evidence, correctness, design, contract and security, each a fresh shadow-reviewer with its own brief in its spawn call, all Agent calls in the same turn.

questions.situation: Code review. 6 files, 2 journeys, a new helper module; nothing sensitive. You can't tell whether it counts as large.
questions.ask: One reviewer or one per lens?
questions.expect: One per lens, in parallel: when unsure, go parallel.

questions.situation: Code review of a large change whose diff includes src/components/ExportButton.tsx and a CSS file.
questions.expect: Yes: the diff touches something the user sees, so ui joins evidence, correctness and design.

questions.situation: Parallel code review, not sensitive. The design lens stopped without writing its reply; you started it once more fresh and it failed again.
questions.expect: Merges the other lenses without it, names it in the notes and tells the user.

questions.situation: `dispatch: orca`. You're starting the coder as an Orca worker for implement.
questions.ask: How does the brief reach it, and where does its reply land?
questions.expect: The brief goes inline as the worker's `--spec`; the worker writes its full reply to `review-output/coder-<n>.md` in the feature folder (created first) and passes it as `--report-path` to `worker_done`, since worker_done carries only a short summary.

questions.situation: Parallel code review of a sensitive change. The security lens failed twice.
questions.expect: Asks the user whether to retry, review that lens yourself, or go on without it; does not silently merge without security.

questions.situation: Merging lens replies. Contract found a minor at src/users.js:14, correctness a major at src/users.js:14, both about the same missing await.
questions.expect: One row, not two: severity major, lens cell `contract, correctness`, status open.

questions.situation: Merging a re-review's lens replies. A lens reports a finding that matches row R2 already in review.md.
questions.expect: It updates R2 instead of adding a row; only genuinely new findings take the next free ids.

questions.situation: review.md has an open major: `Weakened test: the @S3 assertion was loosened from toEqual to toBeDefined`.
questions.ask: Does it go to a fix round?
questions.expect: It goes straight to the user, who picks a fix round, rebutted or deferred; you don't decide it.

questions.situation: review.md has an open blocker R1 and an open major R3 (neither a weakened test). It's the first fix round.
questions.ask: What do you do, and what do the re-review briefs carry?
questions.expect: One fix round with the same coder (continued with SendMessage, not a new one), which replies per finding id; then one re-review, chosen the same way, whose briefs carry the coder's replies and the commit the last review saw.

questions.situation: The user says "continue" in a fresh session. `solodev status` says review, open: R1, R3. progress.md ends with `- review 1 at 3f2a9c1` and `- fix 1: R1 fixed · R3 rebutted: the null check is upstream in parse()`, and the coder's fix is committed.
questions.ask: Do you run a fix round, and what does the next brief carry?
questions.expect: No new fix round: fix 1 is spent. It starts the re-review, chosen as in code review, whose briefs carry the `- fix 1` line (R1 fixed, R3 rebutted with its reason) and 3f2a9c1 as the commit the last review saw.

questions.situation: After the fix round and the re-review, major R3 is still open.
questions.expect: Takes it to the user: another fix round, deferred or dropped, written into review.md. No second fix round on your own.

questions.situation: Re-review. review.md has open row R1 with lens `security`. The fix diff touches only src/users.test.js.
questions.ask: Which lenses run, and what does each get?
questions.expect: The open security row makes the re-review sensitive: security rechecks R1 against the fix diff and evidence runs again at HEAD. It isn't treated as a small test-only change reviewed alone.

questions.situation: Re-review. Row R2 (`contract, correctness`, an ordinary finding) went to both lenses. Contract says fixed; correctness says rebutted, the coder's reason holds.
questions.expect: rebutted, with both reasons written in review.md.

questions.situation: Re-review. Row R4 starts `Weakened test:` and went to evidence and contract. One says fixed, the other rebutted.
questions.expect: It stays open: a Weakened test: row is never rebutted by the lenses.

questions.situation: Re-review with several lenses. Row R5's lens cell says `single` (the first review was one reviewer); it's about an unhandled empty input.
questions.expect: The lens that fits it best: correctness.

questions.situation: You are shadow-reviewer, started from a brief with `lens: security`. You'd like a second opinion on one finding.
questions.ask: Do you start another reviewer? Where do your findings go?
questions.expect: No subagents. Findings go in its reply (the YAML as its final message), not in review.md, which the session that started it merges.

questions.situation: You are shadow-reviewer with `lens: single`. You found nothing.
questions.expect: review.md with the header row alone (the lens column present), recording a clean review, plus the reply with zero counts. The repo stays as it found it.

questions.situation: You are shadow-reviewer on a single re-review. review.md has R6 with status `deferred`, and R7 with status `open` whose text starts `Weakened test:`. The fix diff doesn't touch R7's test; instead the coder's reply rebuts R7 with a sound reason.
questions.ask: What do you mark R6 and R7?
questions.expect: Leaves R6 as it is (the user's decision). R7 can only be marked fixed by the reviewer, so it stays open; rebutted on a Weakened test: row is the user's call.
